title: The AI race is no longer just about who has the smartest model
excerpt: AI's new North Star isn't smarter models. It's delivering the most useful intelligence for every dollar spent.
content_html:
AI's new North Star: Intelligence per dollar

By Alistair Barr

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

Author of the Tech Memo newsletter

The AI industry has spent the past few years obsessing over one question: Who has the smartest model?

That still matters. But a new north star is emerging: how much useful intelligence can be delivered for each dollar spent.

A lot of models are now good enough for many business tasks. Once that happens, buyers start caring less about the absolute best model and more about the cost of getting reliable work done with AI.

Eugene Kim's recent scoop on Amazon's rebuild of Alexa+ is a good example. Internal documents show the company routing more requests to its own less-powerful AI, while avoiding unnecessary calls to Anthropic's pricier, higher-performing models.

The goal was not to make Alexa use the smartest model every time. It was to use expensive intelligence only when the job required it.

"This is a very strong and real trend," said Kylan Gibbs, CEO of Inworld, which develops powerful voice AI. "We're reaching a state where many models are good enough, and in that context, it really becomes about efficiency."

His company has created separate research teams focused on making Inworld models cheaper and faster to run, not just more intelligent.

So, what's the best AI model, per dollar of intelligence? This is harder to answer than when the industry was focused on pure performance. Still, Peter Gostev, AI capability lead at Arena AI, shared four things to consider:

  • How good is it? How reliably does the model complete real work?
  • What does it charge? Compare the cost of both reading a request and producing an answer. Some model providers charge more for especially large jobs.
  • How much can it reuse? Reusing information already processed can dramatically reduce the bill.
  • How much work does it take? A model that's cheap on a per-token basis may still cost more if it needs extra steps or repeated attempts to finish the job.

Peter was reluctant to share a clear ranking of AI models based on these criteria, partly because this trend is so new.

However, this is becoming increasingly clear: The smartest model may still win the headlines, but the model that delivers the most useful work for the money will win the market.

content_html_zh:
人工智能的新北极星：每美元的智能

作者：Alistair Barr 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。 《技术备忘录》时事通讯的作者

过去几年，人工智能行业一直在思考一个问题：谁拥有最聪明的模型？

这仍然很重要。 但一颗新的北极星正在出现：每花一美元就能提供多少有用的情报。

现在许多模型足以胜任许多业务任务。 一旦发生这种情况，买家就会开始不再关心绝对最佳模型，而是更多地关心利用人工智能完成可靠工作的成本。

Eugene Kim 最近对亚马逊重建 Alexa+ 的独家报道就是一个很好的例子。 内部文件显示，该公司将更多请求发送给自己功能较弱的人工智能，同时避免不必要地调用 Anthropic 价格更高、性能更高的模型。

目标不是让 Alexa 每次都使用最智能的模型。 只有在工作需要时才使用昂贵的情报。

“这是一个非常强劲且真实的趋势，”开发强大语音人工智能的 Inworld 首席执行官凯兰·吉布斯 (Kylan Gibbs) 表示。 “我们正在达到一种状态，许多模型都足够好，在这种情况下，它真的变得与效率有关。”

他的公司成立了独立的研究团队，专注于使 Inworld 模型更便宜、运行速度更快，而不仅仅是更智能。

那么，对于每美元的智能来说，最好的人工智能模型是什么？ 与行业专注于纯粹性能时相比，这个问题更难回答。 尽管如此，Arena AI 的人工智能能力主管 Peter Gostev 分享了需要考虑的四件事：

  • 有多好？ 模型完成实际工作的可靠性如何？
  • 它收费什么？ 比较读取请求和生成答案的成本。 一些模型提供商对特别大的工作收取更高的费用。
  • 可以重复使用多少？ 重复使用已经处理过的信息可以大大减少费用。
  • 这需要多少工作量？ 如果模型需要额外的步骤或反复尝试才能完成工作，那么按代币计算便宜的模型可能仍会花费更多。

Peter 不愿意分享基于这些标准的人工智能模型的明确排名，部分原因是这种趋势太新了。

然而，这一点变得越来越明显：最聪明的模型可能仍然会赢得头条新闻，但提供最有用的工作的钱的模型将赢得市场。
